publication_scope.blurb: Ludwig Crocius — Book I Chapter 5 On Sacred Scripture's perfection and sufficiency, from the 1636 Bremen Latin. Densify COMPLETE (PHYS 210–mid-238): perfection defined so nothing may be added or subtracted; three heads (canonical number; authentic-text purity; integrity of lettering / vowel-points); what Scripture contains as necessary; thirteen reasons for perfection; three contradictions (papal traditions; zealots of private consequences; diverting the Church from the Bible); two modes of containing revelation. Cap. 6 On Scripture's clarity begins mid PHYS 238; Cap. 4 complete; the rest of the Syntagma remains.
publication_scope.era_note: Crocius wrote in the early seventeenth century as Reformed professor at the illustrious school of Bremen. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1636 Villerian folio is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
publication_scope.first_english_note: No complete public-domain English of this 1636 Latin Syntagma was locked as reading text. This is a new rendering from locked Latin for Liber I Cap. 5 densify complete.

text_history.method: English follows the locked 1636 Bremen Latin of Liber I Cap. 5 densify COMPLETE, reconstructed from SLUB Dresden page images (PHYS 210–mid-238 before CAPUT SEXTUM). Same-page OCR (tesseract lat + Vision) used as check. No modern English was copied. Cap. 6 (CAPUT SEXTUM / De sacrae Scripturae claritate) begins mid PHYS 238. No Internet Archive copy was located.
